title: Matcha: That Ain't Just Tea
summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about joining Instagram and Gwyneth Paltrow's 2015 matcha latte post, then cover matcha in depth: what it is (powdered, shade-grown green tea leaves, tencha ground into powder), its history from Zen monks and Myoe at Mount Togano, the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu and the Uji region, shading cultivation techniques, the Kyoto tea auction, the grades and growing regions (Uji, Fukuoka, Nishio, Shizuoka), preparing matcha and the tea ceremony (chado), theanine and catechin health claims, antioxidants and free radicals, and caffeine effects. The episode ends with a listener mail from Travis about a fish tapeworm contracted from ceviche.
topics: Stuff You Should Know book announcement

segments.title: Book announcement and Instagram banter
segments.summary: Hosts announce their upcoming book and preorders, then chat about joining Instagram and the Gwyneth Paltrow link to matcha's popularity.

segments.title: What matcha is and how it is made
segments.summary: Matcha is steamed, dried, de-stemmed tea leaves ground into a bright green powder, and the whole leaf is consumed unlike steeped tea. Its name combines the Japanese words for powdered and tea.

segments.title: History and Zen monks of Mount Togano
segments.summary: Matcha's origins trace to tea seeds brought from China by a Zen monk, cultivated by his pupil Myoe at Mount Togano, where natural conditions made good leaves. Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu then pushed expansion to Uji.

segments.title: Grades and growing regions
segments.summary: Ceremonial grade is discussed as a label that may be unreliable. Four Japanese regions produce matcha: Uji (most renowned), Fukuoka, Nishio (largest by volume, mass market), and Shizuoka (largest green tea producer, not well regarded for matcha).

segments.title: Preparing matcha and the tea ceremony
segments.summary: The hosts describe the chado tea ceremony as exact, purposeful and meditative, then give simple home preparation: about half a teaspoon of powder, warm water under eighty degrees, whisked with a bamboo whisk and drunk in about three sips.

segments.title: Shade cultivation and the Kyoto tea auction
segments.summary: Growers shade tea bushes with straw, then aluminum and fabric, starting in mid April to boost chlorophyll and theanine and reduce bitter catechins. Tencha from all producers is auctioned at the Kyoto tea market, where blends are chosen by blind tasting.

segments.title: Health benefits, antioxidants and caffeine
segments.summary: Matcha is linked to benefits including memory, mood, and liver and kidney health. The hosts explain free radicals, oxidative stress and antioxidants such as catechins, plus matcha's calm alertness from caffeine combined with theanine. Milk can reduce the antioxidant effect.

segments.title: Travis's tapeworm listener mail
segments.summary: Listener Travis describes getting a fish tapeworm from ceviche made by a fishing lodge guest, and the treatment and recovery that followed.
